commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the principal argument of z^3 is 300 degrees when arg(z) = 100 degrees, because cubing triples the angle.

fixIt.corrected: Angles wrap around: the principal Arg must land in -180 to 180 degrees, so wrap 300 degrees by subtracting one whole turn: 300 - 360 = -60 degrees, and arg(z^3) = -60 degrees.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: find the principal argument Arg(z^3) when arg(z) = 100 degrees, showing the wrap step in your working.

commonErrors.misconception: If arg(z) = 100 degrees then arg(z^3) = 300 degrees.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks 300 degrees as the principal argument Arg(z^3), defending it as three 100-degree turns.

fixIt.corrected: 300 degrees is the same point as -60 degrees, but it is outside the principal range -180 to 180 degrees: the principal value is Arg(z^3) = -60 degrees.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why 300 degrees is not a principal argument even though it names the same point.

commonErrors.misconception: If arg(z) = 100 degrees then arg(z^3) = 300 degrees.

modelAnswers.answer: The conjugate of z = 2 - 3i is 2 + 3i. Their product is z times its conjugate = 2^2 + 3^2 = 4 + 9 = 13, which is |z|^2.
modelAnswers.question: Find the conjugate of z = 2 - 3i, and calculate the product of z and its conjugate.

nextSteps: Reteach the angle wrap from the paired notes trap before any further complex numbers work: the principal Arg must land in -180 to 180 degrees.
Practise writing the wrap step in the working whenever a multiplied argument passes 180 degrees.
strengths: Most of the class can find a conjugate and its product, such as the conjugate of z = 2 - 3i is 2 + 3i and the product is 13 on the worksheet.
The class can find a modulus by Pythagoras, such as |6 + 8i| = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 on the exit ticket.
